page.layout: One text column with marginal notes in the left margin: "Niceph.1. cap.35." at the top, "Nero." beside the fifth line, "a ex Gallis Sig." beside the fourteenth line, and "Vespasianus Imp." beside the nineteenth line. No notes in the right margin. The catchword "fianus" stands at the foot right.

main_text.p: Niceph.1. cap.35.lare coeperunt. Adversus eos Vespasianus proconsulari imperio a Nerone missus multis gravibusq; praeliis devictos, coegit intra muros Hierosolymæ confugere. In-Nero.terim vero iam etiam sibi pro conscientia scelerū invisus, humanis rebus eximitur: incertum an ipse sibi mortem conscive-rit: certe corpus illius interemptum. Unde creditur, etiam si se gladio ipse transfixerit, curato vulnere ejus servatus, fecū-dum illud quod de eo scriptū est: Et plaga mortis ejus curata est, sub seculi fine mitredus, ut mysterium iniquitatis exerceat. Igitur post excessum Neronis, Galba imperium rapuit: mox Otho, Galba interfecto, occupavit. Tunc Vitellius {a}in Gallias, fretus exercitibus, quibus præerat, urbem ingressus, Othone interfecto, summam rerum usurpavit: quæ postea quam ad Ves-Vespasia-nus Imp.pasianum delata, licet malo exemplo, bono tamen affectu Reip. ab improbis vindicandæ, cum Hierosolymam obsideret, fumit imperium: &, ut mos est, diademate capiti impositō, ab exercitu Imperator confalutatus, Titum filium Cæsarem fecit. Eidem pars copiarum, & obsidendæ Hierosolymæ negotium datum. Vespa-

page.notes: The first word is a fragment ("lare") continuing from the previous page. The marginal note "a ex Gallis Sig." is an inferred reading of the note beside the text mark "a" after "Vitellius". The ligature "fecū-dum" and the hyphen after "conscive-" are as printed. Long s is normalised to plain s throughout. Some margin notes are only partly legible at the scan edge; the readings given are the most likely ones.
